scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
Agent researched a disjoint batch; integration and structural checks are not independent historical certification.
Imported border coordinates remain unchanged. Historical events and map coverage are distinguished in prose; see batchIdentityNotes for conflicts.

proposedOverrides.summary: A changing Labrador atlas umbrella for diverse Innu histories, circa 800 to 1530 CE.

batchIdentityNotes: Coverage calls the record a state, but the card treats that only as database metadata and does not invent one medieval Innu polity.
The exact id, imported-summary provenance, nine coverage intervals, 1492 gap and 1530 label split are preserved and audited.
Innu communities, Innu-aimun dialects, the Naskapi Nation, Inuit neighbors and archaeological complexes remain distinct.
The exact polygons omit every tested Cote-Nord and Saguenay Innu community point, so the card does not present them as comprehensive territory.
Direct archaeology, oral history, later ethnography, community teaching, government history and modern scholarship remain labeled evidence types.
No contemporaneous writing sample is supplied because the documented Innu writing tradition begins after the target interval.
